hero.heading: That Christmas card maker from 2019 can still read your bank statements.
hero.subtitle: You didn't give it permission to do that — you gave it a recipient list. It took your entire drive. Melusina is an operating system where every app runs in its own sealed container on your hardware. Nothing shared unless you choose.

hero.ahaMoment: You gave away your digital life one app at a time. Email here, docs there, photos somewhere else. Melusina brings it all back — onto one server you control.

problem.heading: You gave away your digital life. One app at a time.
problem.intro: It started with email. Then documents. Then photos, passwords, calendars, notes, chat, AI. Each one a different company. A different set of terms. A different copy of your life on a server you'll never see. You didn't plan for this. It just happened.

points.consequence: Gmail because it was easy. Dropbox because it synced. Slack because your team was there. Every choice made sense. None of them were about keeping control.
Your files in one place, your notes in another, your passwords in a third. Try leaving. Exporting from Notion is a research project. Migrating from Google is a month of your life.
Your calendar reads your contacts. Your project tool sees your email. Everything is connected to everything behind the scenes. One breach and it all spills — because nothing was ever truly separate.
One admin holds the keys. One company sets the terms. They can raise prices, change policies, or get hacked. You'll find out after.

problem.punchline: But you can take it back. One server. Your data. Every piece of your digital life — separate, private, yours.
problem.ahaMoment: The tools exist now. The infrastructure is real. It's not too late.

meetMelusina.heading: One place for everything. Everything in its own place.
meetMelusina.subtitle: Melusina is an operating system — like having your own private internet. Install it on a server. Open it in any browser. Every single thing inside it — a document, a conversation, a photo album, a financial plan — lives in its own sealed container. Not because of settings. Because that's how it's built.
keyPoints: It runs on your hardware — a PC, a dedicated server, a cloud VPS. You reach it from any browser on any device.
Every document is its own world. A spreadsheet can't see a chat room. A photo album can't see a tax return. They're physically separate containers — not permission-separate.
When two things need to talk, you decide. A window shows your options. You pick. One connection. Nothing else changes.
Build without coding. Point at the apps you need — documents, identity verification, chat, AI — click them together. Clients see one dashboard. You built it in minutes.
Your whole company can live inside it. Email, documents, code, AI, customer bots, compliance — all apps on one OS. Add what you need when you need it.
Leave whenever you want. Export everything in standard formats. No lock-in. No exit fees. Your data is yours.
meetMelusina.ahaMoment: Think of it like having your own private internet — where every app runs on your box, nothing phones home, and you decide what connects to what.

solution.heading: Three ideas that change everything.
solution.subtitle: Most platforms connect everything and hope nothing goes wrong. Melusina separates everything and lets you connect what you choose.

pillars.title: Separation by Default
pillars.description: Think filing cabinets, not open-plan offices. Every document, every chat, every app lives in its own sealed room. Your personal budget can't see your work project. Client A can't see Client B. A breach in one room stays in one room.

pillars.title: Connection by Choice
pillars.description: When you need two things to talk — and only when you need to — you open a slot between exactly those two things. A spreadsheet that asks one AI model for help. An invoice that connects to one payment method. Nothing blanket. Nothing permanent unless you want it.

pillars.title: No Single Point of Failure
pillars.description: No single password. No single admin. Critical operations require multiple people — like a safe that needs two keys. Someone leaves? One action freezes their access across everything. No chasing down a dozen logins.

isolation.heading: What it feels like.
isolation.subtitle: Not features. Moments.
isolation.intro: The best way to understand Melusina isn't a feature list. It's to picture yourself using it.

layers.title: The moment you need AI
layers.tagline: Your report needs OCR. Nothing else does.
layers.description: You're working on a document and need to extract text from a scan. A window shows your available AI models — local and cloud. You pick one. That document gets AI. Your hundred other documents don't know it happened.
layers.concrete: One choice. One connection. One document. That's the whole model.

layers.title: The moment a client verifies
layers.tagline: They see their passport. You see a verdict.
layers.description: You send a verification link. Your client uploads their passport in their own private space — their own sealed container. AI extracts the data, matches their face, returns a verdict: verified or not. You see the verdict. You never touched the passport.
layers.concrete: Their data in their container. Your review in yours. Physically separate.

layers.title: The moment someone leaves
layers.description: An employee leaves on Friday. You freeze their access — one action. Every document, every tool, every workflow — gone. Monday morning there's on-chain proof of exactly when it happened. No spreadsheets. No chasing twelve different services.
layers.concrete: Their authority was a token. You froze it. Done.

examples.heading: More moments
items: A customer messages your Telegram bot → a support ticket appears in your workflow app. The bot can't see anything else.
Push code to a branch called 'public' → your website is live. No deploy scripts. Git push equals published.
Share a photo album with grandma → 48-hour link. Then it vanishes.
Build a client portal → pick identity verification, documents, chat. Point and click. One unified dashboard.
Your startup runs entirely inside Melusina — email, docs, code, AI, bots, compliance. One OS. One server.

access.heading: The difference
access.description: Traditional: connect Zapier to Stripe — Zapier sees all your Stripe data forever. Melusina: your invoice requests one payment from one payment app. That's all it can do. Revoke anytime.

isolation.callout: Every moment follows the same principle: you choose what connects to what. Nothing happens automatically. Nothing is permanent unless you say so.

features.title: A license anyone can check
features.description: Your Melusina license is an NFT on Solana. The chain is public: Foundation → Reseller → License → your Shares. Any partner, regulator, or client can verify it. No phone calls. No PDFs. Just math.

features.title: Sign in with your wallet
features.description: Browser extension, mobile wallet, or QR code — three ways to authenticate with your Solana wallet. Keyholders get admin access automatically. No passwords to forget.

features.title: Multiple keys for critical operations
features.description: Vault access, certificate rotation, backup decryption — all require multiple keyholders to approve via Solana. One person can't do it alone. That's the design.

features.title: Freeze access in one block
features.description: Admin authority is an NFT. Freeze it — access revoked in the same Solana block. On-chain proof of exactly when it happened.

features.title: Prove what's running
features.description: Check the license on Solana. Verify TLS certificates via DNS. Confirm the Foundation-signed release hash. Anyone can verify your infrastructure without trusting you.

ai.heading: Your questions are your most intimate data.
ai.subtitle: What you ask an AI reveals what you're worried about, what you're planning, what you don't know. With Melusina, those questions never leave your server.

features.title: Private AI that runs locally
features.description: Connect local models or cloud services — each in its own container. Every prompt stays on your server or goes only where you explicitly allow. No training on your data. No harvesting. Proof, not promises.

features.title: AI reaches only what you point it at
features.description: Your document needs OCR? It asks your AI hub and you approve — for that document alone. Your KYC app needs extraction? Same process. One connection per request. The AI never sees your whole world.

features.title: Every query logged. Every model auditable.
features.description: Who asked what, when, which model answered. An append-only audit trail you control. When someone asks 'does your AI see my data?' — show them the architecture. It can't.

items.title: TLS certificates pinned in DNS
items.description: Your TLS certificates are pinned in DNS records signed with DNSSEC. Man-in-the-middle attacks are mathematically impossible. Anyone can verify the pin by querying DNS — no trust needed.

items.title: No persistent secrets
items.description: CA private keys are created from license data when needed, used once to sign a certificate, then destroyed. Vault keys come from keyholder approvals. There's nothing to steal because nothing is stored.

items.title: Nothing starts without verification
items.description: After every reboot: verify the license on Solana, check the release hash, wait for keyholder approval, then start services. Tampered code won't boot.

items.title: Instant admin revocation
items.description: Admin authority is an NFT. Freeze it — access revoked in the same Solana block. No database coordination. No hoping they forgot the password. On-chain proof of when access was granted and revoked.

items.title: Per-app spending limits
items.description: Each Pearl has its own SOL wallet with spending limits. Apps consume platform services — OTP, email, SMS, AI — via micropayments. Operators set budgets. Runaway costs are impossible.

items.title: One server, every screen
items.description: Melusina runs on your hardware — a PC, a VPS, a dedicated server. You open it from any browser on any device. Add it to your home screen for instant access. Push notifications arrive content-free — payloads carry no data. Your server talks to your screen and nothing leaks in between.

points.description: License Registry deployed on Solana. Master NFT minted. 4 keyholders activated. 2-of-4 threshold configured. Full trust chain operational.

points.title: Real cryptography, not toy crypto
points.description: Shamir secret sharing over GF(256) with Lagrange interpolation. Per-keyholder encrypted shares. 44 unit tests verify the implementation. Auditable code.

points.title: Open source since 2014
points.description: Production-proven sovereign infrastructure. We added NFT licensing, threshold crypto, Solana verification, TLS pinning, and local AI. Full source code. Audit every line.

credibility.stat: A growing library of production apps. 4 keyholders. 2-of-4 threshold. 79 boot tests. 72 deployment tests.
credibility.testimonial: "The only platform where anyone — a regulator, an auditor, a partner, a client — can independently verify that the operator's infrastructure is legitimate." — Melusina Foundation

items.question: Is this actually deployed, or just a whitepaper?
items.answer: Deployed. License Registry is live on Solana. Master NFT minted. 4 keyholders activated with 2-of-4 threshold. Full trust chain operational: Foundation → Reseller → License → Shares.

items.question: Do I need to be technical to use this?
items.answer: No. Open it in your browser. Pick apps. Connect them by pointing and clicking. Build client portals, onboarding flows, and dashboards without writing code. Melusina handles isolation and security automatically.

items.question: What if one of our keyholders is unavailable?
items.answer: That's the point of multi-keyholder design. With 2-of-4, any two keyholders can approve operations. One person being unavailable doesn't block anything.

items.question: Can I actually leave if I want to?
items.answer: Yes. Export everything. Your data is in standard formats. Your license is on the blockchain. There's no lock-in. If you want to migrate, you migrate.

items.question: Who is this for?
items.answer: Anyone who's tired of their data being scattered across the internet. A family protecting photos. A journalist protecting sources. A startup protecting IP. A fintech meeting compliance. A DAO running governance. Same OS, same isolation — you just install different apps.
